notes: LDV's only current-generation electric ute (eT60) is included with reasonably solid figures. The eT60's successor, the eTerron 9 (Maxus eTerron 9 globally), has been repeatedly delayed since an original 'early 2025' target; as of Aug 2026 press coverage LDV Australia says it 'continues to work with the factory' with no confirmed on-sale date, so it is EXCLUDED from variants per the 'omit anything not confirmed for Australia' rule (see notes for spec preview). eDeliver 7 pricing is highly inconsistent across sources: LDV's own site advertises a promotional drive-away price for MY23 SWB Low Roof ($54,990 driveaway, ABN-holder offer ending 30 Sept 2026), while CarExpert's 2026 pricing tool shows a base drive-away price of $46,305-$48,411 for one configuration and a wider drive-away band of $61,042-$82,009 across ~12 listed configurations that appear to mix diesel and electric drivetrains inconsistently in the underlying data. Given this inconsistency, eDeliver 7 priceAud is set to null and flagged low-confidence; only body/battery/range specs believed reliable are included. eDeliver 9 pricing and specs are consistent across CarExpert (2022-2023) and LDV's own site and are treated as higher-confidence, though the RRP figures originate from a 2023 launch report un-updated for potential 2026 changes. V2L (Sept 2026 pass): a CarsGuide reviewer's Australian eDeliver 7 test drive explicitly states 'a big disappointment is the lack of V2L or an internal three-pin outlet', so v2l is set to false for both eDeliver 7 variants (flagged low-confidence: single-reviewer source). No V2L feature is mentioned anywhere on LDV Australia's own eDeliver 9 page or in CarExpert's/CarsGuide's eDeliver 9 coverage, consistent with the eDeliver 7 finding for the same manufacturer/generation, so v2l is set to false there too (flagged low-confidence: absence-of-evidence rather than an explicit manufacturer denial). eT60 (Sept 2026 pass): CarExpert's Australian review explicitly wishes for 'a Ford-style vehicle-to-load (V2L) system' to be added, confirming it is not fitted; the ute does have 12V and 220V interior sockets, but that is not full V2L. No later coverage through the 2026 model year indicates this has changed, so v2l is set to false with medium confidence.
